subject: Numeracy
title: Numerals 1 to 10
subtopics: Tracing numerals in sand and air
objectives: Children will recognise the numerals 6 to 10.
Children will trace numerals in sand and in the air.
content: Looking at numerals 6 to 10, tracing numerals in sand and air, and matching numerals and groups.
teachingActivities: Link each numeral to a quantity; model the starting point and direction of each numeral; use sand, clay, large air movements and pipe cleaners before pencils; accept reversed numerals gently; keep sessions short.
learnerActivities: Recognise the numerals 1 to 10 and trace them in sand and air.
resources: A tray of sand or flour
assessment: Observe whether each child names numerals 1 to 10 and traces some of them.
crossCurricular: Literacy: letter-like shapes and fine motor skills

lessons.title: Numerals 6 to 10
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will recognise and name the numerals 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count objects to 10 and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Hold up the numeral 7 and say "This is the numeral seven. It means seven things."
teacherActivities: Show each numeral and count that many counters.
Hide a numeral and ask "Which one is missing?"
learnerActivities: Child places a card by a group.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each numeral and count that many counters. Children: Children count with the teacher.
Step 2. Teacher: Say each numeral name slowly. Children: Children repeat each name.
Step 3. Teacher: Hide a numeral and ask "Which one is missing?" Children: Child says the missing numeral.
Step 4. Teacher: Match numeral cards to groups. Children: Child places a card by a group.

practical.title: Match 6 to 10
steps: Put the card by the group.
practical.safety: Use counters too large to swallow and supervise matching. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Match numerals 6 to 8 only and use the number line.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two numerals that add to ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Hold up each numeral and say it together.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for numerals 6 to 10 on a calendar or clock.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "recognise and name the numerals 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Tracing numerals in sand
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Tracing numerals in sand and air
objectives: Children will trace numerals in sand using a finger.
successCriteria: Traces a numeral with a finger
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count objects to 10 and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
resources: A tray of sand or flour
lessons.starter: Show a tray of sand and say "Today we draw numbers in the sand with our fingers."
teacherActivities: Show how to draw the numeral 1 in the sand.
Say the numeral as you draw it slowly.
Let each child trace a numeral on a card then in the sand.
Smooth the sand and try another numeral.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to draw the numeral 1 in the sand. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Say the numeral as you draw it slowly. Children: Children copy the movement.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child trace a numeral on a card then in the sand. Children: Child traces a numeral.
Step 4. Teacher: Smooth the sand and try another numeral. Children: Child smooths and traces again.

practical.title: Sand numerals
practical.safety: Keep sand low in a tray and wash hands afterwards. Do not let children throw sand or rub eyes.

differentiation.support: Trace over the child’s finger with your hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to write two numerals without a card.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say the numerals.
lessons.homeConnection: Trace numerals in flour or rice with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "trace numerals in sand using a finger" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Numerals in the air
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Tracing numerals in sand and air
objectives: Children will make big numeral movements in the air.
successCriteria: Draws a numeral in the air
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count objects to 10 and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Hold a ribbon and say "Let us draw a big number in the air."
teacherActivities: Show how to draw a large numeral in the air.
Say the numeral as you draw it.
Use ribbons to draw numerals 1 to 5.
Let children choose and draw a numeral.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to draw a large numeral in the air. Children: Children copy with their arms.
Step 2. Teacher: Say the numeral as you draw it. Children: Children say it with you.
Step 3. Teacher: Use ribbons to draw numerals 1 to 5. Children: Child draws with a ribbon.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children choose and draw a numeral. Children: Friends guess the numeral.

practical.title: Big air numerals
steps: Draw a numeral in the air.
practical.safety: Leave plenty of space between children and keep ribbons short. Watch that ribbons do not wrap around necks.

differentiation.support: Draw the numeral beside the child with a large arm movement.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw two numerals in a row.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we use to draw?

lessons.conclusion: Put away the ribbons and say the numerals.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw big numerals in the air with a finger at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make big numeral movements in the air" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Playdough numerals
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make numerals from playdough and match them to groups.
successCriteria: Puts the matching number of counters
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count objects to 10 and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Show a numeral made from playdough and say "I can roll and shape a number."
teacherActivities: Show how to roll a snake and shape it into a numeral.
Let each child make a numeral from a card.
Put the matching number of counters by it.
Say "This is a six. Six counters."
learnerActivities: Children say the numeral and count.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to roll a snake and shape it into a numeral. Children: Children roll playdough.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child make a numeral from a card. Children: Child shapes a numeral.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the matching number of counters by it. Children: Child counts and places counters.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "This is a six. Six counters." Children: Children say the numeral and count.

practical.title: Playdough numbers
practical.safety: Use non-toxic playdough and check for allergies. Keep playdough away from mouths and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Shape the numeral together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make two numerals and compare.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and show your numeral.
lessons.homeConnection: Make numerals with playdough or clay at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make numerals from playdough and match them to groups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 numerals check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how well each child recognises and traces numerals.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count objects to 10 and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Sing the numeral song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: sand, air and playdough.
At each station ask "What numeral?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: sand, air and playdough. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What numeral?" and watch. Children: Child names and traces numerals.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Numeral stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep sand and playdough away from eyes and mouths. Wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use numerals 1 to 5.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to write numerals with a pencil.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names numerals 1 to 10; traces numerals in sand; makes numerals; matches numerals to groups.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.homeConnection: Keep spotting numerals in daily life.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how well each child recognises and traces numerals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
